verdict.rationale: Linear's Loops let users describe a recurring job in plain language and choose a schedule or event trigger, with no code required. One documented example chains steps: when a project's target date changes, a loop updates the launch plan and posts a Slack message. However, the evidence is limited to changelog snippets, there is no documented builder for explicit step sequencing, conditions or branching, and a community user (an older report) described workflow automation as Linear's weakest area, needing Zapier or custom integrations. missing for 10: in-depth docs on composing multi-step workflows (step sequencing, conditions, available actions), a visual or no-code builder description, hands-on corroboration that Loops reliably run multi-step automations.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can build multi-step automations without writing code

citations.quote: Loops are a new way for Linear Agent to take on recurring work for your team. Describe the job in plain language and then choose whether it should run on a schedule or in response to an event.
When a project's target date changes, a loop can automatically update the launch plan and post a Slack message explaining what changed, why, and who needs to act.
Loops are recurring agent workflows for teams. They now respond to more workspace activity, including changes to initiatives, projects, and cycles.
